targets.text: The fleet dashboard has a Boundaries tab: an operator reads every machine's memory-guard boundaries and their live state, and creates, changes and deletes them from the page, without logging in to each box (issue #18)
Every acceptance criterion of issue #18 maps to a confirmed claim in this frame or is listed as out of scope

fleet_reader passes each daemon's mem_guard through to /api/fleet, mesh status and the MCP machine_state, tolerating its absence on daemons older than 0.17 (today extract() keeps only THERMAL_FIELDS, heat_governor/fleet_reader.py:79-98,225-243; mesh.py _row whitelists columns)
A daemon document without mem_guard still yields state ok, and the history ring and /api/history are unchanged

The daemon's mem_guard document gains what the page shows and /state lacks today: each boundary's matchers (comm, cmdline, cgroup) and source file, plus act_over_pct, max_kills_per_hour and min_victim_mib. Today an entry is exactly name, max_mib, scope, usage_mib, state (memboundary.py:165-172; docs/contracts/state.md:52), and adding keys is allowed ('clients ignore unknown fields')
docs/contracts/state.md documents every added mem_guard key, and a client that reads only the 0.17 keys still works

The config loader merges [[memory.allow]] rules from a sibling boundaries.toml into [memory] before validation, rejects a name that appears in both files, watches both files' mtimes, and keeps the last good boundaries when only that file is invalid (today load() reads one path, Config.path/mtime are scalars, changed() compares one mtime: config.py:885-909, daemon.py:502-540)

A name present in both config.toml and boundaries.toml is rejected with a message naming both files, and an invalid boundaries.toml keeps the last good boundaries while a valid config.toml edit still applies

A stdlib emitter writes the boundaries.toml [[memory.allow]] shape, escaping control characters and newlines in matcher strings, and the write is atomic (temp file + os.replace) with a backup. No emitter exists: _toml_value (config.py:924-935) handles scalars/lists only and escapes only backslash and double quote; config init --write is a plain write_text (tuning.py:120)
Emitting any valid rule set and loading it back with tomllib yields the same rules, including matchers containing quotes, backslashes and non-ASCII; a failed write leaves the previous file intact

A new boundaries CLI noun (overview, list, add, set, rm, a stdin apply used by the remote write, and a preview) follows the agent-first contract: register() in cli/__init__.py, overview verb and bare-noun overview, explain catalog entry, learn text, overview._VERBS line, --json and exit codes
uv run teken cli doctor . --strict passes and explain resolves every boundaries path

The SSH and local transports gain one fixed, argv-only write path that can send a body on stdin and return the remote exit code and stderr (the validator's message), with its own timeout and a defined way to find heat-governor on the remote box
The remote command is a fixed argv with the rule data only on stdin, never interpolated into the command string, and the validator's message reaches the caller verbatim

mesh serve accepts boundary writes: method dispatch for POST/PUT/DELETE, a capped JSON body reader, a bearer token compared in constant time (401 on a bad token, 403 when none is configured), Origin and Content-Type checks, If-Match with 409 on a stale version, and 4xx error mapping. test_post_not_allowed, the read-only docstrings and the mesh serve help text change with it
With no token file every write is refused with 403 and GET responses are byte-for-byte what they are today; tokens are compared with hmac.compare_digest and never logged

The daemon, not the CLI, emits memory_boundary_changed when it reloads a changed boundaries file, and the kind joins recorder.MEMORY_EVENTS so it is recorded and shipped; the reader keeps its own audit log (token label, time, machine, old and new rule) in its state dir
A boundaries change made by hand on the box also produces memory_boundary_changed, and the reader's audit log is append-only with mode 0600

A preview runs on the target box: memprocs.scan + memboundary.assess for within/over/far_over per matching process, with the killer's names function, uid, protect list, min_victim_mib and action deciding whether a far-over process would really be killed; command lines pass through redact() and the container column comes from container_id(cgroup)
The preview and the live guard agree: for the same process table and rule, the preview's state and killable verdict equal what MemKiller decides

The Boundaries tab is built inside heat_governor/web/index.html as a second view of the one React/htm page: a hash-routed Sections nav (Machines | Boundaries) in the header, reusing the existing classes (.pills button[aria-current], .chip, .status, .tag, .facts, .dt, .search, .eyebrow, .lede, Mark/rune, useFleet) and the html[data-mode] theme, not the design's .app.dark class or its anchor-styled pills
tests/test_web_page.py still passes, #machines renders exactly as today, and the page loads nothing from another origin

New styles are limited to what the dashboard does not have yet: buttons (.btn, primary, danger), icon buttons, form fields (input, select, label, hint, error state), a usage bar with boundary and far-over marks, a left-aligned rules table, and a modal confirmation dialog; the design's inline stroke SVG icons (plus, pencil, bin, lock, warning, refresh) are a new vocabulary for the page
Every new control is a real button, input, select or label reachable by keyboard, and the modal traps focus and closes on Escape
The page stays self-contained: Lato from /vendor, no Google Fonts link (the design's helmet loads fonts.googleapis.com), no new vendored library, no third-party runtime dependency, CSP unchanged
pyproject.toml dependencies stays [] and the CSP string in mesh_server.py is unchanged

The page covers states the design does not draw: a machine that is unreachable or stale, a daemon with no mem_guard (older than 0.17 or guard off), action = record (a far-over process is not killed), a save that fails or times out over SSH, a validator rejection for any field (the design shows it for max_mib only), and a rule whose max_mib is under min_victim_mib (blamed, never killed)
Each listed state has a rendering covered by a page test or a fixture document

The page edits boundaries.toml rules only: it never changes [memory] action, act_over_pct, limits, [ship] or thermal settings, and rules written in config.toml show read-only (issue #18 Safety and Out of scope)
The write endpoint and boundaries apply accept only [[memory.allow]] rule fields; any other key is rejected by the validator

GET /api/fleet, /api/history and the Machines view keep their behaviour, and remote daemons keep listening on loopback only, reached over the reader's SSH link (issue #18 acceptance criteria and Out of scope)
The existing mesh server, fleet reader and transport tests pass unmodified except test_post_not_allowed
The operator of the six-box fleet who opens the mesh serve dashboard on the EliteMini, and agents that read the fleet through heat-governor mesh status, the MCP tools and the boundaries CLI
The page, mesh status --json, the MCP machine_state tool and boundaries list --json all return the same boundary data for a machine

Boundaries are [[memory.allow]] rules hand-edited in each box's config.toml over SSH; no box has one configured; the dashboard, mesh status and the MCP tools show no memory-guard data at all, and mesh serve is read-only and unauthenticated
On 2026-11-15 /api/fleet on the EliteMini reader carried no mem_guard key and tests/test_mesh_server.py::test_post_not_allowed asserts POST is refused

The dashboard has a Boundaries tab listing, per machine, the guard's action, limits, kills and every boundary with its matchers, usage and state; with a write token the operator adds, changes or deletes a boundaries.toml rule on any machine from the page or from heat-governor boundaries, sees which running processes it matches before saving, and the daemon applies it on its normal live reload
A rule created from the page on one machine is visible in heat-governor boundaries list --machine M and in that machine's /state without any manual step on the box

All six boxes run action = kill with no boundaries, so known large workloads (vLLM near full memory on thor and the sparks) are judged by growth alone; setting boundaries per box by hand is slow and unreviewed, and a wrong rule can make the guard kill a process
docs/deliveries/2026-11-14-memory-guard.md:117 states 'No [[memory.allow]] rule is configured on any box yet'
After PR 1, /api/fleet returns mem_guard for all 6 machines and the Boundaries tab shows each machine's guard state within 1 poll of the reader
A test feeds a /state document with and without mem_guard through fleet_reader.extract and gets the key through unchanged or absent, never an error

After PR 2, a rule saved from the page on a local and on an SSH machine appears in that machine's mem_guard.boundaries in under 15 s, a write with no or a wrong token gets 403 or 401, and a stale version gets 409 with nothing written

Tests cover 401, 403, 409 and a successful write through a fake transport and a localhost server, and the live check on one SSH box is recorded under docs/evidence before the write path is called live

The reader runs the remote write and preview by an explicit binary path, default ~/.local/bin/heat-governor with a per-machine override key in fleet.toml, and the on-box command writes boundaries.toml beside the config file the running daemon reports in /state (config, daemon.py:1061), not beside whatever the SSH shell's environment resolves (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
On every fleet machine the write succeeds with heat-governor absent from the non-interactive SSH PATH, and a daemon started with --config elsewhere gets its boundaries.toml beside that file

The reader refuses a write to a machine whose daemon version predates boundaries.toml support, with a message naming the version needed, and the page shows that machine as read-only until it is upgraded; a missing remote boundaries verb is reported as that same refusal, not as 'unreachable' (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
A write aimed at a 0.17.x daemon is refused before any file is touched on the box

The version check and the write are one atomic step on the box: the on-box command takes an exclusive lock, compares the caller's base version with the hash of the file as it is now, and only then writes; the reader never decides a conflict on its own copy (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
Two concurrent applies with the same base version produce exactly one success and one conflict, and a hand edit between read and save is reported as a conflict

The editor's rule list and base version come from the boundaries.toml file read on the box, not from /state, and the reader passes through the daemon's config path and config_error so the page can say when the file on disk was rejected and the daemon is still running the last good rules (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
With an invalid boundaries.toml on a box the page shows the rejection message and the last good rules as live, and an edit starts from the file's content

A change that only touches boundary rules does not lose the guard's detection state: the fill-rate window and the kill budget survive it, either by swapping the rules in the running guard or by carrying the trigger window across the rebuild (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
A test saves a boundary while a simulated runaway is filling memory and the trigger fires no later than it does without the save

The kill confirmation is enforced on the box, not only drawn in the page: the on-box apply re-runs the preview at write time and refuses a change that would put a killable own-user process far over its boundary unless the request explicitly allows it, returning the processes concerned (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
An apply without the allow flag that would make a running own-user process far over writes nothing and returns that process; the same request with the flag writes

The validator rejects a boundary whose matchers are all bare wildcards, and the preview reports how many processes a rule matches, because a rule that matches everything with a large maximum makes every process 'within' and so switches the guard off for that box (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
A rule with cmdline = '*' and no other matcher is rejected with a message, on the page and in the CLI

Every endpoint that returns process command lines or accepts a change requires the token, including the preview; the token travels only in the Authorization header, never in a URL; mesh serve refuses to start with a token file readable by group or others; write requests are refused when the Host header is not the address the server listens on (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
An unauthenticated request to the preview endpoint gets 401 or 403 and no process data, and a token file with mode 0644 stops mesh serve with an error

A save whose response is lost is not left ambiguous: writes are whole-rule and idempotent, and after a timeout the page re-reads the file version and reports saved, not saved or conflict from what is on the box (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
With a fake transport that applies the write and then times out, the page ends in 'saved' and a repeat of the same request changes nothing

Recovery is specified: each write keeps a timestamped backup of the previous boundaries.toml, at most 5 are kept, and the contract documents how to restore one; deleting boundaries.toml is a valid state that means no page-managed rules (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
After 7 writes exactly 5 backups exist and restoring the newest one reproduces the previous rules after a reload

The daemon remembers the hash of the boundaries it last applied in its state dir and emits memory_boundary_changed at startup when the file differs, so a change made while the daemon was down or restarting is still recorded and shipped (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
Stopping the daemon, changing boundaries.toml and starting it again yields one memory_boundary_changed event with the old and new rules

Writing a boundary changes a live machine: the first live write on any box, enabling a token file on the EliteMini mesh unit, and any test or probe against a real box need the user's go-ahead; tests use tmp_path config dirs, a fake transport and fake /proc trees and never write under a real ~/.config or signal a process they did not spawn (challenge pass, 2026-11-15)
CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md and QWEN.md carry this rule next to the existing run --apply and [memory] action rules, and no test touches the real config directory

the note records which boxes were upgraded, to which version, and any machine that did not report mem_guard
tasks.instruction: Upgrading daemons and restarting the mesh unit changes live machines: ask the user before each step. Read-only otherwise. File devague evidence for obligation o16 with the outcome, pass or fail.

tasks.summary: PR 2: the config loader merges a sibling boundaries.toml, watches both files and rejects match-all rules
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_config_memory_allow.py: rules from config.toml and boundaries.toml are merged before validation, each tagged with its source file; a name in both files raises ConfigError naming both files
an invalid boundaries.toml keeps the last good boundaries and publishes the message in config_error, while a valid config.toml edit made at the same time still applies
touching only boundaries.toml triggers a reload within reload_every_s; deleting it means no page-managed rules; boundaries.toml accepts only [[memory.allow]] tables and rejects any other key
a rule whose matchers are all bare wildcards raises ConfigError, in either file
tasks.instruction: Owns heat_governor/config.py (load, Config, changed, _validate_allow*) and the reload bookkeeping in heat_governor/daemon.py maybe_reload (lines 502-540) only. boundaries.toml sits beside the config path actually loaded (Config.path.parent), never a path re-derived from the environment. Config.mtime becomes a pair. Config.memory builds MemoryRule positionally (config.py:355-370): keep field order.

tasks.summary: PR 2: boundaries.toml emitter and locked, versioned, backed-up writer
acceptance_criteria: emit then tomllib.loads returns the same rules for matchers with quotes, backslashes, newlines, control characters and non-ASCII

write(base_version, rules) under an exclusive lock compares base_version with the sha256 of the current file; a mismatch writes nothing and returns the current rules; two concurrent writes with one base yield exactly one success

a successful write goes through a temp file and os.replace, leaves a timestamped backup of the previous file, and never keeps more than 5 backups; a failure midway leaves the previous file byte-identical
tasks.instruction: New module heat_governor/boundaries_file.py and tests/test_boundaries_file.py; touch no other file. Stdlib only (fcntl.flock on a sibling lock file, hashlib, os.replace). The version of a missing file is a fixed sentinel so 'create' also conflicts correctly. Validate rules with config's existing allow validators before writing. All tests under tmp_path.

tasks.summary: PR 2: a boundary-only change keeps the guard's fill-rate window and kill budget
acceptance_criteria: tests: after Daemon.set_memory with a MemoryRule that differs only in allow, the trigger's sample window and the killer's budget state are the same as before
a simulated runaway on a fake /proc fires no later with a boundary save in the middle than without one
a change to any other [memory] field still rebuilds the guard as today
tasks.instruction: Owns heat_governor/daemon.py set_memory (lines 767-781) and heat_governor/memguard.py. Prefer swapping the rule set inside the running guard under its lock; carrying the Trigger window across a rebuild is the fallback. No real /proc, no real signals.

tasks.summary: PR 2: the daemon records and ships memory_boundary_changed, including changes made while it was down
acceptance_criteria: a reload that changes the merged boundary rules emits exactly one memory_boundary_changed record with old and new rules, written by the recorder and submitted to the shipper (fake S3)
the daemon stores the hash of the boundaries it last applied in its state dir; starting with a different file emits one event, starting with the same file emits none
docs/contracts/memory.md lists the event in the event table and the ship table
tasks.instruction: Owns heat_governor/recorder.py (MEMORY_EVENTS), the event emission in heat_governor/daemon.py apply_config/_route_memory_event, docs/contracts/memory.md and tests/test_recorder_memory.py. The CLI never records events; the daemon is the only emitter, so a hand edit is covered by the same path.

tasks.summary: PR 2: on-box preview of a draft rule against running processes
acceptance_criteria: on a fake /proc tree, each matching process's state equals memboundary.assess and its killable verdict and reason equal MemKiller.refusal for the same table, rule, uid, protect list, min_victim_mib and action
the result carries the number of matching processes, each with pid, uid, user name when resolvable, redacted command line, container id from container_id(cgroup), anonymous memory and state
the preview uses the killer's names function, so comm matching agrees with the live guard
tasks.instruction: New module heat_governor/mempreview.py and tests/test_mempreview.py. Pure function over memprocs.scan(proc_root) output; expose the killer's names function from memkill.py if needed but change no behaviour there. Never signals anything.

tasks.summary: PR 2: the boundaries CLI noun (overview, list, add, set, rm, apply, preview) on the local box
acceptance_criteria: every verb takes --json, writes results to stdout and errors to stderr, exits 0/1/2 per cli/_errors.py; the bare noun prints the overview; explain resolves every boundaries path; uv run teken cli doctor . --strict passes
apply reads one JSON request on stdin (base version, operation, rule), accepts only name, comm, cmdline, cgroup, max_mib, scope, and rejects anything else with the validator's message and no write
apply re-runs the preview at write time: a change that would put a killable own-user process far over its boundary writes nothing and returns that process unless the request sets allow_kill
list, apply and preview act on the boundaries.toml beside the path given by --config, and list returns the rules with their file version
tasks.instruction: New heat_governor/cli/_commands/boundaries.py and tests/test_cli_boundaries.py; wire register() in cli/__init__.py, ENTRIES in explain/catalog.py, learn.py text and JSON list, overview.py _VERBS. add/set/rm are thin wrappers that build the same request apply takes. Follow memory.py for the noun pattern and add boundaries to the parametrised noun test in tests/test_cli_memory_ship.py.

tasks.summary: PR 2: transports can run the fixed remote boundaries commands with a body on stdin
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_transport.py with the fake ssh: the remote argv is identical for any rule content, the body arrives on stdin, and the caller gets exit code, stdout and stderr instead of Unreachable for a non-zero exit
the command starts with the machine's binary path, default ~/.local/bin/heat-governor, overridable by a bin key in fleet.toml, and passes --config with the path the daemon reported in /state
the write has its own timeout, separate from the 5 s fetch timeout; fetch() and history() behave exactly as before
tasks.instruction: Owns heat_governor/transport.py, heat_governor/fleet.py (MACHINE_KEYS gains bin), docs/fleet.example.toml and tests/test_transport.py. acceptance_criteria: a write to a machine whose reported version is below the first boundaries release is refused before any transport call, with the needed version in the message
every write through the service appends one line (label or user@host, time, machine, old rule, new rule, outcome) to an append-only audit file with mode 0600 in the reader state dir

heat-governor boundaries list|add|set|rm --machine M goes through this service, and its list --json equals the boundary data in mesh status --json and MCP machine_state for that machine

tasks.summary: PR 2: mesh serve accepts token-guarded boundary reads, previews and writes
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_mesh_server.py: with no token file every write and preview gets 403; a missing or wrong token gets 401; a token in the query string is ignored; a stale If-Match gets 409 with the current rules; wrong Origin, Host or Content-Type is refused; bodies over the cap get 413
mesh serve --token-file reads label = token lines, exits 2 if the file is readable by group or others, compares with hmac.compare_digest and never logs a token
every GET that exists today returns the same status and body as 0.17.1, and all existing mesh server, fleet reader and transport tests pass unedited apart from test_post_not_allowed
tasks.instruction: Owns heat_governor/mesh_server.py, heat_governor/cli/_commands/mesh.py (the --token-file flag and help text) and tests/test_mesh_server.py. Routes under /api/boundaries/MACHINE, where MACHINE is a fleet machine name. Add method dispatch and a JSON body reader; map service errors to 4xx explicitly instead of the catch-all 500. Update the read-only wording in the docstrings and help. Token fixtures in tests must pass scripts/scan-secrets.py.

tasks.summary: PR 2: the boundary editor sub-view and modal confirmations in the dashboard
acceptance_criteria: the hash routes #boundaries/MACHINE/RULE (a machine name and a rule name) and a new-rule route open a full sub-view with the form beside a live preview and a back link; rules from config.toml show as read-only
the form's rules and base version come from the file read on the box; a rejected file on disk shows its message with the last good rules marked as live

delete, a change that would kill a process, and a conflict each open a modal dialog with focus handling and Escape to close; without a token the page offers a token field and stays read-only; the token is kept for the tab session only and sent only in the Authorization header
every action is a button, input, select or label with an accessible name; validator messages show for any field; a failed or timed-out save ends in saved, not saved or conflict after a re-read
tasks.instruction: Owns heat_governor/web/index.html and tests/test_web_page.py. Source design: artifact FZzmdU4yBpTbboV4WFUX7x, boards Edit.dc.html and Confirm.dc.html. Process names is a list input (comm is a TOML list). The kill warning states the real conditions: own user, not protected, at least min_victim_mib, action = kill, acted on within about 12 s. New CSS: buttons, icon buttons, fields, modal. Inline stroke SVG icons are allowed; no new vendored file.

tasks.summary: PR 2: contract, working rules, harness files, version bump and changelog for the write side
acceptance_criteria: docs/contracts/boundaries.md documents the file, the merge and collision rule, the request shape, versions and conflicts, backups and how to restore one, tokens, the audit log and the event; docs/contracts/state.md and docs/integration.md are updated

CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md and QWEN.md state that live boundary writes and enabling a token file need the user's go-ahead and that tests never write under a real config directory
